newsitem.title: USA: Ill Gov. named in new Tollway class action lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Ill Gov. named in new Tollway class action lawsuit.

text.p: Illinois taxpayers challenging State Toll Highway Authority budget practices have filed a new state court complaint naming Gov. Jim Edgar, Transportation Secretary Kirk Brown, board members and vendors as defendants.

Filed late Thursday in Cook County, the lawsuit seeks to make the officials personally liable for any misappropriated funds and put vendors on notice they might not get paid and may have to return money already received.
The complaint seeking class action status also names three vendors: Unisys Corp, Envirodyne Engineers Inc and Consoer Townsend Envirodyne Engineers Inc.
Attorney Lee Schwartz said the challengers will seek to have the complaint now assigned to Cook County Judge John Madden consolidated with a case pending before Judge Stephen Schiller.
Schiller in May overturned the Toll Authority practice of allocating its more than $300 million budget without oversight of the governor or General Assembly.
Schwartz and Myron Cherry had sought to add the officials to the case before Schiller, but the judge denied the effort on Aug. 6 for fear it would misdirect the proceeding.
The complaint contends the officials and vendors could no longer defend Toll Authority expenditures as made on good faith at least since Schiller's ruling.

In addition to Edgar and Brown, the lawsuit names Toll Authority Chairman Julian D'Esposito Jr., Executive Director Ralph Wehner, Chief Financial Officer Nicholas Jannite, Controller Mark Swidergal and eight board members as defendants.

Schiller has given Toll Authority officials until Dec. 15 to comply with his court order or be enjoined from all expenditures except for debt service on the agency's nearly $1 billion of outstanding debt.

Rating agencies have raised credit concerns based on Schiller's ruling and the Toll Authority and the trustee for the agency's bondholders, First National Bank of Chicago, a unit of First Chicago NBD Corp, have appealed the finding to the Illinois Supreme Court.
